entries.title: Every clip has its own page — source, transcript, shares and download
entries.summary: Opening a clip in **Media → Clips** now shows a page of its own: the player, the **Source recording** it was cut from, the speaker, the part of the transcript inside the clip (click a timestamp to jump there), and its **Shares** and **Clicks**. **Download** saves the MP4 under the clip's name, and **Add to gallery** puts it in a content gallery. A clip that is still rendering says so and turns playable on its own.

enable.path: Early Access → Preview → Marketing (Clips)

where.path: Marketing → Media → Clips → a clip

entries.use_case: A marketer can hand a finished clip to the social team — download it, check how often it has been shared and clicked, and drop it in the on-demand gallery — from one page, without going back into the editor.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks how to download a clip, where a clip came from, or how a clip is performing.
internal.who_should_get_it: Everyone on the Marketing preview who exports clips.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Media → Clips → a clip. Staff also see **Send to Dispatch** there; it is super-user only, like the Dispatch wizard, so do not show it to customers.
internal.gotchas: To change the cut, the customer still re-exports from the source recording's editor — the clip page has no editor. The transcript empty state on a clip now points to the source recording instead of mentioning Goldcast.

entries.title: Turn an audio recording into an audiogram
entries.summary: An uploaded audio file now has **Export audiogram** under **Actions**: pick a window of up to 10 minutes, a **Shape** (**1:1**, **9:16** or **16:9**), a **Look** (**Brand**, **Dark** or **Light**) and a caption style, and Sessionboard renders a waveform video with burned-in captions and the speaker's name. It lands in the clips library as **Audiogram · *recording title***.

enable.path: Early Access → Preview → Marketing (Clips)

where.path: Marketing → Media → an audio recording → Actions → Export audiogram

entries.use_case: A podcast or an audio-only session has no picture to clip. An audiogram gives it a shareable video for LinkedIn and other feeds, with captions for people watching with the sound off.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer with podcasts, audio-only sessions or MP3 uploads asks how to promote them on social.
internal.who_should_get_it: Marketing preview customers who upload audio.
internal.gotchas: The recording needs a stored file: an RSS-only podcast that was never uploaded is refused. The render has no headshot and uses static captions only (Clean, Bold, Boxed).

entries.title: Uploads get clip suggestions on their own, and every insert reaches the export
entries.summary: Once an uploaded recording's transcript is ready, chapters and suggested clips now appear in the editor by themselves — no **Generate** click, no reload. In the editor, **Insert** adds an image or logo, a text callout, a B-roll cutaway and **background audio**; **B-roll & audio** sets where each B-roll starts and each track's volume. All of them, and your transcript corrections, are burned into the exported clip, including with Animated caption styles.

enable.path: Early Access → Preview → Marketing (Clips)

where.path: Marketing → Media → a recording → Edit & clip

entries.use_case: A marketer uploads a session and finds clips waiting when the transcript finishes, adds the sponsor's logo and a music bed, fixes a misheard name in the transcript, and the exported clip has all of it — no second pass in another video tool.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer says their uploaded recordings never got suggestions, that a logo or callout was missing from an exported clip, or that a corrected word still showed wrong in the captions.
internal.who_should_get_it: Marketing preview customers who cut clips.
internal.gotchas: Pasted transcripts get no automatic suggestions — Generate still works there. Background audio plays only in the export, not in the editor preview, and is not applied to spliced Edit-by-transcript exports. Overlays in Animated caption styles need the current caption render bundle to be active; static styles do not.

entries.title: Large uploads pick up where they stopped after a reload
entries.summary: If you reload or close the tab during an upload, add the same file again on **Media → Import** and it resumes from the parts already sent instead of starting over. An unfinished upload can be resumed in the same browser for up to a week.

enable.path: Early Access → Preview → Marketing

where.path: Marketing → Media → Import

entries.use_case: A 40 GB conference recording takes an hour to upload. A dropped connection or an accidental reload at 80% no longer means starting the hour again.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer uploading large recordings worries about leaving the tab open, or reports an upload that restarted.
internal.who_should_get_it: Marketing preview customers who upload recordings.
internal.gotchas: Resuming needs the same file in the same browser — another computer, or a file with the same name but different contents, starts a new upload. After a week the partial upload expires and the app says so.

entries.title: Attendees can share that they're going with Advocacy
entries.summary: **Attendees** is now an audience in Advocacy. Pick it in Quick Launch and every confirmed or checked-in attendee from your registration platform who has not opted out of marketing gets a personal "I'm attending" card — their name, company and the sessions they registered for — and a tracked link. Put each attendee's link in your registration platform's confirmation email; there is no login.

enable.path: Apps → your registration platform → attendee sync on; then Marketing → Advocacy → New campaign → Attendees

where.path: Marketing → Advocacy → New campaign → Build → Who's sharing → Attendees

entries.use_case: Attendees telling their network they're going is the most credible registration driver an event has. This turns every confirmation email into a share card and attributes each click to the attendee who posted.

cs_action.note: The customer's registration platform team has to add the link to the confirmation email. Help them build it from the campaign id and their platform's registrant id and email merge fields (runbook: sessionboard-tam docs/integrations/attendee-advocacy-install.md).

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks how to get attendees, not only speakers, promoting the event — or is evaluating attendee-referral tools.
internal.who_should_get_it: Events with an Apps Engine registration connection that syncs attendees (Cvent, Swoogo, Swapcard, Visit, LiveBuzz, Bizzabo, Expo Platform).
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Advocacy → New campaign → Attendees. The tile is disabled until the event has synced attendees.
internal.gotchas: Every platform except Swapcard needs `?e=<registrant email>` on the link; send it for Cvent too (a Cvent id alone only works when it is a random v4 uuid). Grip has no attendee source yet, so Grip links always show the not-found page. Cvent needs `event/attendees:read` on its token — most live Cvent tokens are program-only. The on-click fetch for a just-registered attendee is declared for Cvent, Swoogo, Visit and LiveBuzz but only Visit has been live-verified. Advocacy does not email attendees, and the confirmation-page widget is not in production yet.

entries.title: Choose where a content gallery's embargo applies
entries.summary: The gallery **Embargo** settings have a new **Where it applies** section: **Gallery site**, **Website embed** and **Mobile app**. Untick a place to show everything there as soon as an item is visible, while the embargo still holds everywhere else. At least one place stays ticked, and with all three ticked the embargo covers everywhere, as before.

enable.path: Early Access → Preview → Content Galleries

where.path: CMS → Content Galleries → a gallery → Access → Embargo → Where it applies

entries.use_case: A society can open abstracts in its member app ahead of the session while keeping them off the public gallery site and the embed on its marketing website until the presentation.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer with an embargoed scientific program wants a different release time for one channel (the app, their website, the gallery).
internal.who_should_get_it: Content Galleries preview customers who use embargo.
internal.gotchas: Narrowing an embargo is not a security boundary: an unticked place is public, and the UI warns about this. Download protection still treats the embargo as covering everywhere. The website embed only identifies itself after the embeds release (sessionboard-embeds#110) is in production.

entries.title: Copy a gallery's embed code from its Settings
entries.summary: A gallery's **Settings** tab now has an **Embed on your website** card: under **Show**, pick **All items** or one collection, then **Copy code**. The snippet already carries your gallery's slug and your region, so it works when pasted on any page of your own site.

enable.path: Early Access → Preview → Content Galleries

where.path: CMS → Content Galleries → a gallery → Settings → Embed on your website

entries.use_case: A customer's web team gets a working snippet in one click instead of hand-assembling one from the docs, and it points at the right region automatically.

cs_action.note: The Help Center snippet used to name embeds-prod-us / embeds-prod-eu, which do not resolve. Any customer who copied it has a widget that never loaded — send them the code from this card.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks how to put their gallery on their own website, or says the gallery embed shows nothing.
internal.who_should_get_it: Content Galleries preview customers with their own website.
internal.gotchas: A draft gallery's embed shows an error until the gallery is published. If the URL slug was edited but not saved, the card keeps the saved slug and says so.

entries.title: Gallery session pages show the recap you published
entries.summary: When you publish a session's recap, its page in a content gallery now shows it under the description — the recap you approved, never the unreviewed AI summary. It stays hidden while the item is embargoed.

enable.path: Early Access → Preview → Content Galleries

where.path: Published content gallery → a session item

entries.use_case: Someone who missed the session reads the edited takeaways right next to the recording, so the gallery page answers "was this worth watching?" on its own.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer publishing recaps asks where attendees see them, or wants their on-demand gallery to carry more than the abstract.
internal.who_should_get_it: Content Galleries customers who also publish recaps.
internal.gotchas: Only published recaps appear; a session with just an AI summary shows no recap section.

entries.title: Link each Grip session to its recording and summary
entries.summary: Map the new **Summary URL** session field to a link-type custom field in Grip and every synced session gets a clickable link to its public page — its item in a published content gallery, or otherwise its page on your published Attendee Hub. When a session has neither, the next sync clears the link.

enable.path: Integrations → Grip → Map session fields → Summary URL → a Grip link field

where.path: Integrations → Grip → Map session fields

entries.use_case: Attendees browsing the agenda in the Grip app can go straight from a session to its recording and recap, so the event content keeps working after the day.

cs_action.note: The customer has to create a link-type custom field in Grip first and map Summary URL to its Field System Name.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A Grip customer asks how to send recordings or recaps to Grip, or why links in session descriptions vanish.
internal.who_should_get_it: Grip customers with a published content gallery or Attendee Hub.
internal.gotchas: Grip strips links from descriptions — only link-type custom fields keep them. There is no replay URL field to map; Summary URL is the canonical link. Hidden gallery items are never used.

entries.title: Speakers Gallery session pop-ups use your field labels
entries.summary: In the **Speakers Gallery** embed, opening a speaker's session showed custom session fields under their raw key (for example *Qa_multi_limit*). The session pop-up now shows each field's name, or the custom label you set in the embed's **Field Options**.

where.path: Speakers Gallery embed → a speaker → a session

entries.use_case: Visitors browsing speakers on the event website read "Audience" or "Level", not an internal field key.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports odd, capitalised field names in the Speakers Gallery session pop-up.
internal.who_should_get_it: Anyone using the Speakers Gallery embed with custom session fields.

entries.title: Every Pipeline column shows its cards
entries.summary: The **Pipeline** board loaded one batch of cards for the whole board, so on a busy pipeline the first stages took it all and later columns looked empty. Each column now loads its own cards, and a column with more than it shows reads **Showing *n* of *total*** with a **Show more** button.

where.path: CRM → Pipeline

entries.use_case: A team sourcing a large speaker roster sees every prospect in Contacted and Approved, not only the ones in the first column.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer says later Pipeline stages are empty or the board seems to stop at 50 cards.
internal.who_should_get_it: Speaker CRM customers with large pipelines.
internal.gotchas: The per-stage total counts only active entries; deleted submissions are excluded.

entries.title: SSO configurations save with Domain left empty
entries.summary: Saving a SAML, OIDC or OAuth2 configuration with the optional **Domain** left empty failed with a pattern error. It now saves; spaces around a domain are trimmed, and an invalid one gets a clear message — *Enter a domain like example.org, or leave Domain empty.*

where.path: Settings → SSO → Identity Providers → SAML / OIDC configuration → Domain

entries.use_case: An association connecting an identity provider that members use from many email domains can leave Domain empty, as the form says it may, and save.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports a "must match pattern" error when saving an SSO configuration.
internal.who_should_get_it: SSO customers setting up or editing an identity provider.
internal.gotchas: A configuration with no domain is never picked by email-domain discovery, and Domain is still required for admin login.

entries.title: New Advocacy "attending" widget for registration confirmation pages
entries.summary: A new **advocacy-attending** embed widget can be placed on registration confirmation pages. When a registrant lands on the page, the widget prompts them to share the event through Advocacy. The email address is transmitted only as a SHA-256 hash — no cookies or local storage are used.

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to enable the advocacy-attending embed; then add the widget script to your registration confirmation page

where.path: Registration confirmation page (external) → advocacy-attending embed widget

entries.use_case: Capture the moment a registrant confirms their spot and immediately invite them to share the event through Advocacy — turning every new registration into a potential referral without requiring cookies or storing personal data.

cs_action.note: The widget script must be added to the customer's registration confirmation page by their web team; Sessionboard Support or CSM provides the embed snippet.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to drive registrations through peer sharing or wants to activate Advocacy at the point of sign-up.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers running Advocacy campaigns who control their own registration confirmation page.
internal.gotchas: Requires the web-api W13 PR (JSON entry route, CORS allow-list, per-surface embargo) to be deployed first; do not surface to customers before that companion PR is live.
internal.talk_track: Right after someone registers is the best time to ask them to share — this widget does that automatically, with no cookies or stored data.

draft.docs_gap: The Advocacy guide should add a section explaining how to install and configure the advocacy-attending embed widget on a registration confirmation page, including the embed hosts (embeds / embeds-eu / embeds-me.sessionboard.com) and the privacy model (SHA-256 hashed email, no cookies).
draft.why_use_it: When someone completes registration they are at peak excitement about attending your event — the ideal moment to ask them to spread the word. The advocacy-attending widget sits on your confirmation page and surfaces an Advocacy share prompt right then, using only a hashed version of the registrant's email so no personal data is stored in the browser. This means you can activate word-of-mouth at the highest-intent moment in the registration flow while staying aligned with privacy best practices.

entries.title: Regenerating a recap after editing the transcript uses the edited transcript
entries.summary: Clicking **Regenerate with AI** on a recap with no instruction re-summarizes from the transcript when it was edited after the last summary, instead of reusing the old summary.

where.path: Marketing → Transcribe → Recaps → a recap → Regenerate with AI

entries.use_case: A team that corrects names and terms in a transcript gets recaps that reflect the corrections.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer edited a transcript and the regenerated recap ignored the edits.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers publishing Live Transcribe recaps.
internal.gotchas: With an instruction typed in, Regenerate always writes a new recap, as before.

entries.title: Team Lead approval cards show readable labels instead of raw argument keys
entries.summary: The **Team Lead** approval card now displays human-readable rows such as **Form name: Abstract Form**, **Collects: abstract**, and **Collect speaker details: Yes** instead of truncated argument keys (`SubmissionC… abstract`) or raw JSON. Labels wrap to a new line rather than cutting off at 80 px.

where.path: Team Lead → Assistant panel → Approval card

entries.use_case: When Team Lead asks for approval before taking an action, organizers can now read exactly what it is about to do — form name, field being collected, yes/no options — without decoding truncated argument names or raw JSON blobs.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer mentions that Team Lead approval cards are confusing or show garbled text.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using Team Lead / AI Event Agents.
internal.staff_path: Team Lead → Assistant panel → any pending approval
internal.gotchas: Requires the matching sessionboard-agents and sessionboard-web-api PRs on the same branch for full labelled details; the UI degrades gracefully to humanized args on older service versions.
internal.talk_track: Team Lead now shows you plain English on every approval card — no more decoding truncated keys or JSON — so you always know exactly what you're approving before you click.

draft.docs_gap: The Team Lead guide should add a section describing what the approval card shows and how to read each labelled row before confirming or rejecting an action.
draft.why_use_it: Before approving a Team Lead action, you need to know what it will actually do. Previously the approval card showed internal argument keys clipped to 80 px and raw JSON for nested values, making it impossible to verify the request at a glance. Now each row carries a plain label and a readable value — for example "Form name: Abstract Form" or "Collect speaker details: Yes" — so you can confirm or reject with confidence. On older service versions the card falls back to humanized argument names and omits internal IDs automatically.

entries.title: Team Lead names new submission forms and shows plain-language confirmation cards
entries.summary: When you ask **Team Lead** to create a submission form, it now uses the title you gave it (e.g. "Abstract Form") instead of a generic numbered default. Every write or destructive action also shows a plain-English **confirmation card** — replacing the raw API description and argument keys that appeared before — so you can see exactly what will happen before you approve it.

where.path: Team Lead panel → any write or destructive action confirmation card; Program → Session Forms

entries.use_case: Organizers who ask Team Lead to create a submission form now get a form named exactly as they requested, and every action that changes data shows a readable confirmation sentence — not raw API text — before anything is committed.

cs_action.note: Ships automatically for all customers using Team Lead with Sessions 2.0. No configuration needed.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer mentions that forms created via Team Lead had confusing names, or that the confirmation dialog looked like developer documentation.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using the AI Event Agents (Team Lead) feature with Sessions 2.0 enabled.
internal.gotchas: Sessions 2.0 must be enabled on the event for create_session_form to work; the name fix and approval copy are otherwise transparent.
internal.talk_track: Team Lead now names forms exactly as you ask and shows you a plain confirmation before making any changes — no more cryptic API text in the approval step.

draft.docs_gap: The Team Lead guide should add a section explaining what the confirmation card looks like for write actions, including how arg labels are displayed and how to read them before approving.
draft.why_use_it: When you tell Team Lead to create a new submission form called "Abstract Form," the resulting form now carries that name rather than a generic placeholder like "Session Submission Form #3." Before any write or destructive action runs, Team Lead shows you a plain-English confirmation card — for example, "Create a new abstract submission form called 'Abstract Form'" — along with labelled rows for the key settings, so you know exactly what you are approving. This removes the guesswork that came from seeing raw argument names and internal API descriptions in the confirmation step.

entries.title: The Site sign-in page is fully translated, and form links bring visitors back to the form after sign-in
entries.summary: The Site sign-in page appears fully in English, German, Spanish or French, including its banner messages. A signed-out visitor who opens a link to a form that needs sign-in sees sign-in start, and after the magic link lands on that form — even if the link opens in a new tab.

where.path: Your Site → Sign in

entries.use_case: International speakers sign in without a page that is half in English, and nobody loses the form they were trying to open.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer’s non-English visitors see English on the sign-in page, or visitors end up on the Site home instead of the form after signing in.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers with Sites in German, Spanish or French, or who share direct form links.
internal.gotchas: The Site landing page also loads faster (one site lookup instead of two), but has not reached the mobile Lighthouse target.

entries.title: Awards rounds can exclude conflicted reviewers from assignment
entries.summary: In an awards round’s settings, **Privacy & conflict of interest** offers **When a conflict is detected → Exclude from assignment** to every organizer, and the setting saves. A reviewer who has declared a conflict is then left out when reviewers are matched to submissions by category. The assignment shortfall warning gives the real pair and capacity numbers, and imported entries land in the program’s first round so they can be assigned.

enable.path: Awards → a program → Rounds → a round → Settings → Privacy & conflict of interest → Enable COI declarations → When a conflict is detected

where.path: Awards → a program → Rounds → a round → Settings

entries.use_case: An awards program with strict judging rules keeps conflicted judges off the entries they declared, without someone checking every assignment by hand.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks how to stop conflicted judges reviewing entries, or says round settings would not save.
internal.who_should_get_it: Awards customers whose reviewers declare conflicts of interest.
internal.gotchas: The exclusion applies to category-matched assignment. Evaluation-plan rounds are unchanged — their conflict rules live on the plan.

entries.title: Team Lead removes an approval card that is no longer waiting on you
entries.summary: When an approval in Team Lead has already been handled, the chat replaces its card with the message saying so, instead of leaving an **Approve** button that does nothing.

where.path: Assistant panel (Team Lead) → an approval card

entries.use_case: People working with Team Lead only see approvals that still need them.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer says the Approve button in Team Lead did nothing.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using Team Lead actions that ask for approval.
internal.gotchas: The cause — a sub-agent checkpoint overwriting the main conversation’s pending approval — is fixed in sessionboard-agents #125, which deploys separately from this UI change.

entries.title: Automations: step list shows what each email does, and team-member recipients load and keep their names
entries.summary: In the automation builder, the step list shows each saved action’s summary instead of “Send email · Not set”. In a **Send email** action, the **Team members** picker lists the event team before you search, and saved recipients show their names after a reload. The training video library search keeps every key you type.

where.path: Automations → an automation → Then → Send email → Team members

entries.use_case: A team that emails colleagues from automations can see at a glance who each step notifies and pick them without guessing names.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer’s steps all read “Not set”, the team picker is empty until they search, or recipients show as “Team member #…”.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using automations that email their own team.
internal.gotchas: The team picker excludes portal-only users. An Assign reviewers test run with no record now reports Skipped instead of Failed.

entries.title: Site builder: a searchable Open a form picker, and drafts that keep the changes you reverted
entries.summary: In the Site builder, the **Open a form** picker on a button is searchable by form or event name and shows each form’s event, so it stays usable with hundreds of forms. Saving a draft replaces the stored draft, so a setting you changed back (such as the hero background) is not restored from an older draft. Interest forms open for submissions show as open on the Site.

where.path: Site → builder → a button → Open a form; Save draft

entries.use_case: An organization with a large catalogue of forms can link the right one from its Site in seconds, and an editor’s draft looks the way they left it.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer cannot find a form in the Site builder picker, says a reverted setting came back, or an open interest form shows as closed.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers building Sites, especially with many forms.
internal.gotchas: Connecting a custom site domain now returns a specific error when Cloudflare refuses it, instead of a bare server error.

entries.title: Rooms layout on Site program pages: no “Capacity 0”, and it scrolls inside the page on phones
entries.summary: On a Site program page using the **Rooms** layout, a room with a capacity of 0 shows no capacity line instead of “Capacity 0”. On narrow screens the day tabs and room columns scroll inside the layout instead of widening the page.

where.path: Your Site → a program page with the Rooms layout

entries.use_case: Attendees browsing the program by room on a phone get a page that fits the screen.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer’s Rooms page shows “Capacity 0” or breaks their layout on mobile.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers whose Site shows the program in the Rooms layout.
internal.gotchas: A capacity of 0 is treated the same as no capacity.

entries.title: Bulk edit no longer shows a false failure after 60 seconds
entries.summary: When a **Bulk Edit** job takes longer than 60 seconds, the overlay now releases and a "still processing" toast appears instead of an error. Polling continues silently in the background for up to 15 minutes and refreshes the grid when the job finishes. Tree-type custom fields now save and display correctly in the session grid. The **API Tokens** page tells customers to contact their CSM or support when AI is disabled, rather than showing a broken staff-only link. The SSO email-conflict error page now shows a clear, translated explanation instead of a generic configuration error. Missing translation strings across the product are restored in English, French, Spanish, and German.

where.path: Sessions → grid → Bulk Edit; Organization Settings → API Tokens; SSO login page

entries.use_case: Organizers running bulk edits on large session sets no longer see a misleading failure toast after 60 seconds — the job keeps running in the background and the grid refreshes automatically when it completes. Tree fields, SSO error messages, and several UI labels that were blank or showing raw keys are also corrected.

cs_action.note: All fixes are default-on; no configuration required.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports that bulk edit appears to fail on large session sets, that tree fields are saving as plain text, that the API Tokens AI-disabled banner shows a broken link, or that SSO login shows a confusing error on email conflict.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using bulk edit on large session lists, tree custom fields, SSO with email-conflict scenarios, or API Tokens with AI disabled.
internal.gotchas: fr/es/de translation strings for the new locale keys are machine-authored and have not had native-speaker review yet (SB-9870 follow-up). The same 60-attempt polling cap exists in bulk delete and src/lib/jobPolling.ts and is not yet fixed (SB-9860 follow-up).
internal.talk_track: Bulk edit on big session lists used to show a false failure after a minute — it now tells you the job is still running and updates the grid when it finishes. We also fixed tree fields saving incorrectly, a confusing SSO error screen, and several missing UI labels.

draft.docs_gap: The bulk-edit guide should note that large jobs run in the background after 60 seconds and that the grid refreshes automatically on completion.
draft.why_use_it: When you bulk-edit a large number of sessions, the job can take more than a minute. Previously the overlay would close with what looked like an error, leaving you unsure whether the changes were saved. Now the overlay releases after 60 seconds with a clear "still processing" message, polling continues quietly for up to 15 minutes, and the grid refreshes automatically once the job is done — so you can keep working without worrying about the outcome. Tree-type custom fields also now save and render correctly in the session grid, and the SSO email-conflict screen shows a plain-language explanation in your language instead of a cryptic configuration error.

entries.title: Contact support now routes through Team Lead, with a live-chat handoff when needed
entries.summary: **Header → Help → Contact support** (renamed from **Message Support**) now opens the Team Lead panel, which tries to resolve the issue first. When Team Lead determines a human agent is needed, it opens a HubSpot live-chat thread automatically and shows a **Chat with Support** card to reopen it. The HubSpot widget loads only on org and event admin pages; it no longer appears in Account Settings or on the account home page.

where.path: Header → Help → Contact support

entries.use_case: Organizers who need help can now get an immediate answer from Team Lead without waiting for a human agent; if Team Lead can't resolve it, the live-chat thread opens automatically so they reach the support team in one flow.

cs_action.note: A HubSpot setting change is required: turn off the SEVA AI agent on the Support chatflow so it routes straight to the Help Desk inbox. Without this, the handoff may still hit the retired AI agent.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to reach support, or reports that the old Message Support button is missing from Account Settings or the account home page.
internal.who_should_get_it: All customers — the change is default-on for every org and event admin page.
internal.staff_path: Header → Help → Contact support (on any /org/:id or /event/:id page)
internal.gotchas: The HubSpot widget no longer loads on Account Settings or the account home page, so customers who bookmarked those pages to reach chat will need to navigate to an org or event page first. Upsell buttons for Exhibitors Pro, Sponsors Pro, and Groups Pro now go through Team Lead instead of opening HubSpot directly.
internal.talk_track: Team Lead now handles your first line of support — it answers common questions instantly and escalates to a live agent automatically when needed, so you spend less time waiting.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should document the new Team Lead → live-chat handoff flow, explain that the HubSpot widget is only available on org and event admin pages, and note that the entry point is now labelled Contact support (not Message Support).
draft.why_use_it: When you click **Contact support**, Team Lead asks what's wrong and tries to resolve it on the spot using its knowledge of your event. If it can't, it hands off to a live support agent by opening a HubSpot chat thread automatically — you don't have to find a separate chat widget. A **Chat with Support** card stays in the conversation so you can reopen the thread at any time. This replaces the previous direct-to-chat button, giving you faster answers for common questions while still connecting you to a human when you need one.

entries.title: Advocacy video and image cards render again
entries.summary: Advocacy videos and image cards generate again; renders had been failing since October 6. If a video cannot be created, the speaker sees a short message instead of a technical error, and uploading an empty preview thumbnail says “Preview thumbnail is empty” instead of failing.

where.path: Marketing → Advocacy; the speaker’s Creator Companion and Portal Home

entries.use_case: Speakers get the personalised video and card they were promised to share, which is the point of an Advocacy campaign.

cs_action.note: Every Advocacy video and image render failed from Oct 6 until this deploy. Customers who launched or edited a campaign in that window should be told renders work again; staff can re-trigger failed renders once new ones complete.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer or speaker reported a video or card that never generated, or a download that failed, between Oct 6 and this release.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers running Advocacy campaigns with video or image templates.
internal.gotchas: One video template still needs its thumbnail backfilled after deploy (engineering task). A creator override that names a removed background is dropped silently.

entries.title: Sending-domain setup catches misspelled domains, can be cancelled, and event Domains show the inherited sender
entries.summary: Setting up a custom sending domain flags common misspellings such as `gmial.com` or `sessionboard.con` as you type and names the likely fix. A setup that is still waiting on DNS has a **Cancel setup** button, with a confirmation. An event’s **Domains** tab shows the organization sender it inherits, and an address that was set up before Domains existed shows **In use** instead of **Not set up**.

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to enable Custom Sending Domain for the organization; then Settings → Domains

where.path: Settings → Domains (organization and event)

entries.use_case: An admin setting up branded email catches a typo before handing DNS records to IT, and can start over without a support ticket if the address was wrong.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer is setting up a sending domain, typed the wrong one, or asks which address an event sends from.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers with the Custom Sending Domain add-on.
internal.gotchas: Only known misspellings are flagged; a real look-alike domain still passes. A verified domain cannot be cancelled — see “Go back to the default sender” in the guide.

entries.title: Public API returns when a participant’s acceptance invitation was sent
entries.summary: Session participants in the Public API include `acceptance_invite_sent_at` — when the acceptance invitation was last sent, or `null` if it has not been sent.

enable.path: Settings → Record Settings → Participant Acceptance → Enable Participant Acceptance and Save; then the Invitations and deadlines panel

where.path: Public API → sessions → participants

entries.use_case: A team that tracks speaker confirmations in its own CRM or a reporting tool can see who has been invited, and when, without checking Sessionboard by hand.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer integrating through the Public API asks how to tell whether a participant has been sent an acceptance invitation.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using Participant Acceptance who read sessions through the Public API.
internal.gotchas: The value is null until the first invitation; integrations should handle null.

entries.title: Changing a campaign’s card design refreshes its thumbnail on Portal Home
entries.summary: Saving a card design in **Edit campaign** re-renders the Advocacy card thumbnail, as **Quick Launch** does when a campaign is created, so Portal Home shows the current design instead of a blank or old image.

where.path: Marketing → Advocacy → a campaign → Edit campaign → card design; Portal Home

entries.use_case: A marketer who tweaks a live campaign’s card sees speakers get the new design straight away.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer edited a campaign card and Portal Home still shows the old or a blank image.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers running Advocacy campaigns.
internal.gotchas: Depends on the render fix in the “Advocacy video and image cards render again” entry.

entries.title: Removing a contact warns about sponsor and exhibitor access, and Merge Duplicates pre-selects the right people
entries.summary: The **Remove** dialog for a contact lists the sponsor or exhibitor access they will lose, and the removal is recorded in History. **Merge Duplicates** pre-checks only the contact you are viewing and rows with the same email, not the three highest-scoring matches.

where.path: CRM → Contacts → a contact → Remove; CRM → Contacts → a contact → Merge Duplicates

entries.use_case: An admin cleaning up contacts sees what a removal takes away before confirming, and does not merge people who only look alike.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer removed a contact and a sponsor lost a portal user, or merged contacts that were not duplicates.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers with sponsor or exhibitor portals, and anyone deduplicating contacts.
internal.gotchas: Customers used to the old top-three pre-selection will see fewer rows ticked; that is intended. A merge with an invalid primary or source contact now fails up front with a clear error.

entries.title: Participant Acceptance: reminders the same day, no sends after the deadline, clearer send results
entries.summary: An invitation sent late in the day gets its first reminder before the day ends in the event’s timezone, instead of waiting 24 hours. **Send** and **Resend** are blocked once a participant’s **Accept by** date has passed, until you extend it. The invitations table on a session has an **Awaiting response** filter, deadlines read in words instead of a code, and the send summary counts and labels people who **already responded** separately from blocked rows.

enable.path: Settings → Record Settings → Participant Acceptance → Enable Participant Acceptance and Save; then the Invitations and deadlines panel

where.path: Program → Sessions → a session → Acceptance invitations; Program → Sessions → select → Send invitations

entries.use_case: A team chasing speaker confirmations gets every invitee reminded on time and cannot accidentally invite someone after their deadline.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer says first reminders never went out, invitations were sent after a deadline, or the send summary called responders “blocked”.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using Participant Acceptance.
internal.staff_path: Participant Acceptance is enabled per event under Record Settings.
internal.gotchas: Extending the deadline re-enables Send for that participant. Someone already invited is still not emailed again unless the organizer chooses Resend.

entries.title: Set org-wide e-signature defaults from Contract settings
entries.summary: A **Settings** button on **CRM > Contracts** opens **Contract settings**: the **Default way to send** (which tab Add Contract opens on), **Signing link expiry** (1–365 days), **Automatic reminders** cadence (1–30 days), the **Organization countersigner** who signs countersigner roles, the **E-signature consent text** shown on the signing page, and the **Auto-advance on contract completion** stage shared with Docusign. Each control shows the built-in default beside the current value; blank means use the default.

enable.path: Preview (bottom of the organization sidebar) → Contracts → Request access; your customer success manager turns it on

where.path: CRM → Contracts → Settings

entries.use_case: Admins who send contracts at scale can set a single countersigner, expiry window, and reminder cadence once at the org level instead of configuring each contract individually — ensuring every contract goes out consistently.

cs_action.note: Walk the customer through the countersigner and consent text before their first send — the defaults work, but a named countersigner and their own consent wording are usually wanted.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to standardize their contract workflow — countersigner, reminder cadence, or expiry — across their whole team.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer actively using Contracts (preview) who sends contracts to multiple speakers or sponsors.
internal.gotchas: Read-only without the manage-app-connections permission. Consent text changes apply to contracts sent from then on; contracts already out keep the wording they were sent with.
internal.talk_track: Instead of each sender picking their own expiry and reminder settings, you can lock in org-wide defaults once and every contract will follow them automatically.

entries.title: Send contracts for e-signature with Sessionboard e-sign — no Docusign account needed
entries.summary: **Add Contract** now has a **Send with Sessionboard** tab: pick a published template, check the ordered **Signers** list (filled from the record, your organization countersigner, or typed in when a role calls for it), optionally pick the event for branding and variables, and **Send for signature**. Each signer gets an email with a personal link to a branded signing page where they review the PDF, fill their fields, draw or type a signature, agree to the e-signature consent, and sign or decline; templates can sign in order or all at once. When the last signer finishes, Sessionboard stamps the signatures, appends a signing certificate, stores the PDF on the record as **Signed**, emails every signer a copy, and can auto-advance the pipeline entry. Contract rows show signer progress (**0 of 2 signed · waiting on …**) with an expandable **Details** panel — signers with statuses and timestamps, decline reason, reminder count, template version, void reason, recent activity — and **Resend reminder** and **Void** (with an optional reason) work for Sessionboard and Docusign contracts alike. Signers who have not signed are reminded automatically on the org's cadence.

enable.path: Preview (bottom of the organization sidebar) → Contracts → Request access; your customer success manager turns it on

where.path: CRM → Contacts (or Accounts / Groups / Pipeline) → record → Contracts → Add Contract → Send with Sessionboard

entries.use_case: Teams that send speaker, sponsor or exhibitor agreements can now collect signatures without a Docusign subscription: the agreement is filled from the record, each signer signs in their browser, and the completed PDF with its signing certificate lands on the record automatically.

cs_action.note: Contracts is a Beta hand-raise: the customer clicks Request access under Preview, CS enables it on the org. During the Beta CS also creates the customer's e-sign templates (the Templates page is SB-9815; until it ships, templates are created through the templates API with the customer's agreement text) — the Send with Sessionboard tab shows "No published templates" until one exists.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks whether Contracts needs Docusign, is paying for Docusign only for speaker agreements, or wants to see who has and has not signed without opening another tool.
internal.who_should_get_it: Contracts Beta customers without a Docusign account, and Docusign customers who want ordered multi-signer agreements tracked on the record.
internal.staff_path: Org → Early Access → Contracts (Beta); templates via POST /contracting/organization/:orgId/templates/native until SB-9815
internal.gotchas: Document-mode templates only — PDF-mode (upload a finished PDF and place fields) is Phase 2 (SB-9821/9822). The participant portal's Sign Now still opens Docusign only; Sessionboard e-sign signers sign from the emailed link until SB-9818. Admin screens are English-only (SB-9854); the signing page is localized. Reminders run on the jobs worker (ENABLE_CONTRACTING_NATIVE_REMINDERS is set in prod).
internal.talk_track: Write the agreement once as a Sessionboard template, send it from the speaker's record, and the speaker, your countersigner and anyone else sign in order from a branded page — no Docusign seat, and you can see exactly who is holding things up.

entries.title: A friendly payment reminder banner appears 7 days before an invoice is due
entries.summary: A light blue **Payment reminder** banner now appears for every org user starting 7 days before an invoice's due date. It shows the due date, a countdown ("due in 3 days", "due tomorrow", "due today"), and a **View invoice** link for users with billing access. The banner can be dismissed for 24 hours and is tracked separately from the past-due banner, so dismissing the reminder never hides the escalation banners that appear after the due date.

where.path: Organization — top-of-page banner (visible on all org pages)

entries.use_case: Org admins and their team get a heads-up before an invoice goes past due, giving them time to arrange payment without triggering the escalating warning banners that follow the due date.

cs_action.note: Enabled automatically for all orgs with an upcoming invoice due date. No configuration required.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks why they are seeing a blue banner at the top of their org, or when following up on overdue invoices.
internal.who_should_get_it: All customers — the banner is shown to every org user whenever an invoice is within 7 days of its due date.
internal.staff_path: The staff Payment due card describes the new 7-day timing window.
internal.gotchas: Dismissal is stored per-banner type: snoozing the reminder does not suppress the past-due escalation banner that appears the day after the due date. Users without the View Billing Details permission see the billing contact email instead of the View invoice link.
internal.talk_track: Starting 7 days out, your whole team sees a friendly heads-up so you can pay before any escalation kicks in — and dismissing it for a day won't hide the more urgent banners if the invoice goes past due.

draft.docs_gap: No existing guide covers the payment reminder banner or the billing escalation banner sequence; a new section in a Plans & Billing guide should document the 7-day reminder, the countdown text variants, the dismiss/snooze behaviour, and how it relates to the post-due escalation banners.
draft.why_use_it: When an invoice is approaching its due date, every member of the organization sees a clear, non-intrusive reminder so nothing slips through the cracks. The banner counts down the days and links directly to **Plans & Billing** for anyone with billing access, or to the billing contact for everyone else. It can be snoozed for 24 hours without affecting the separate past-due escalation banners (blue → yellow → orange → red) that appear after the due date. This gives your team a 7-day window to act before any escalation begins.

entries.title: A resumed call-for-papers draft opens where the submitter left off and keeps what organizers added
entries.summary: Reopening a saved submission draft lands on the first step that is not finished — **Session** or **Participants**, not always **Your Information** — and **Review** flags every incomplete card. The draft shows values an organizer saved on the session after the draft was started, such as an uploaded file. The form’s default status is applied when the draft is submitted, and the “Leave site?” prompt appears only when there are unsaved changes.

where.path: Portal → Call for Presentations → a saved draft

entries.use_case: Submitters who finish a proposal over several sittings pick up at the step that still needs them, which means fewer half-finished drafts at the deadline.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer says submitters are lost when they return to a draft, organizer uploads vanish from drafts, or submitted drafts got the wrong status.
internal.who_should_get_it: Every customer whose call for papers allows saving drafts.
internal.gotchas: An organizer opening the form while signed in as admin now sees the submitter’s draft instead of an “another user’s draft” message. The submitter’s own later re-save still wins over an organizer’s value. Re-editing an already-submitted session keeps its status.

entries.title: A friendly payment reminder banner appears 7 days before an invoice is due
entries.summary: A new **upcoming payment** banner now appears in the 7 days leading up to an invoice due date, giving organizers advance notice before the past-due escalation begins. The reminder can be dismissed and shows how many days remain until the due date. The stricter past-due banner still appears the day after the due date, unchanged.

where.path: Organization billing banner (top of screen)

entries.use_case: Organizers who are approaching a payment deadline now see a clear, non-alarming reminder with days remaining, so they can act before the account enters a past-due state.

cs_action.note: Rolls out automatically; no configuration needed. The past-due escalation path is unchanged.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks why they are seeing a new banner before their invoice is due, or when discussing billing communication improvements.
internal.who_should_get_it: All customers with active invoices approaching their due date.
internal.gotchas: The banner is dismissible, so a customer may not see it again after dismissing even if the due date has not passed. The past-due banner still fires the day after the due date regardless of dismissal.
internal.talk_track: You now get a heads-up 7 days before an invoice is due so you can pay before the account shows past-due — and you can dismiss it once you've seen it.

draft.docs_gap: No existing guide covers the billing banner or invoice due-date notifications for organizers; a short section on billing reminders and the past-due escalation path should be added to a billing or account-settings guide.
draft.why_use_it: When an invoice is coming due, you now see a dismissible reminder banner up to 7 days in advance, including how many days remain. This gives you time to arrange payment before the stricter past-due notice appears. The reminder uses a calm, informational tone — it is not the escalated past-due message — so you can address it without urgency. The past-due banner continues to appear the day after the due date, exactly as before.

entries.title: Interest forms: Speakers Only confirmation wording, Open form for signed-in visitors, more question types
entries.summary: A **Speakers Only** interest form’s confirmation page says “Speaker Proposal” (in English, German, Spanish and French) without flashing the session wording first. **Open form** on a public Site page starts a new submission straight away for a visitor who is already signed in. Date, time, date-time, currency and radio speaker questions appear on the form. Assigning a submission to an event carries its **Format** and **Track** across, and the form builder’s **Preview** shows help text formatted.

where.path: Site → an interest form and its confirmation page; CRM → Interest Forms → form builder → Preview; CRM → Pipeline → Assign to event

entries.use_case: Speakers applying through a standing interest form get the right wording and every question the organizer asked, and the team does not retype Format and Track after assigning.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports wrong wording on a Speakers Only confirmation, signed-in visitors bounced to sign-in, missing question types, or Format/Track lost on assign.
internal.who_should_get_it: Speaker CRM customers publishing interest forms on a Site.
internal.gotchas: Format and Track carry across by label: the event needs a Format or Track with the same name as the organization library option.

entries.title: Reviewer portal: primary presenter star on parent sessions, and Build sessions filters apply to your abstracts
entries.summary: In the reviewer portal, the participant list of a parent session shows the **primary presenter** star. In **Build sessions**, the sidebar filters now narrow **Your assigned abstracts**, so the pool updates when you change a filter.

where.path: Reviewer portal → My Reviews → a round → a parent session; Build sessions

entries.use_case: A reviewer building sessions from a large abstract pool can filter down to one track or format and see who leads each session without opening it.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A reviewer says Build sessions filters do nothing, or cannot tell who the primary presenter is on a parent session.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers whose reviewers build sessions from abstracts (reviewer session builds), and plans that evaluate parent sessions.

entries.title: Leave the event date out of automated emails while your schedule is unconfirmed
entries.summary: Turn on **Hide event dates in emails** in **Settings → Record Settings → Dates & IDs** and the automated emails Sessionboard sends for the event — submission confirmations, evaluation invitations and reminders, receipts — leave out the event date, including where a template uses the event date merge tag.

enable.path: Settings → Record Settings → Dates & IDs → Date & Time → Hide event dates in emails

where.path: Settings → Record Settings → Dates & IDs

entries.use_case: A team that opens its call for papers before the dates are final can send confirmations without printing a date it may have to correct later.

cs_action.note: Off by default; organizers turn it on per event.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer’s dates are provisional, or they want to stop the date appearing in submission confirmations.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers who open a call for papers or evaluation before the event dates are confirmed.
internal.staff_path: Settings → Record Settings → Dates & IDs → Date & Time. Changes are written to History.
internal.gotchas: Only Sessionboard’s automated emails read this setting. Email campaigns the customer writes, and any date typed into a template by hand, are unaffected.

entries.title: Portal pages no longer show "Request failed" errors for events without Speaker Feedback
entries.summary: Admins and speakers viewing author or submitter portals on events that do not have **Speaker Feedback** enabled were seeing red **"Request failed"** error banners on every portal page. The portal config now correctly exposes whether Speaker Feedback is active, so the feedback-flags request is only made when the feature is on; and the flags endpoint itself now returns an empty "disabled" response instead of a 403 for orgs without the feature, clearing errors for any browser tabs already open.

where.path: Portals → any speaker or submitter portal

entries.use_case: Any event team whose portal users were seeing red "Request failed" banners on every portal page will have those errors cleared automatically — no action needed.

cs_action.note: Fix is automatic and default-on. No customer action required. The 403 errors on portal pages should be fully resolved after this deploy.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports red 'Request failed' banners appearing on every portal page, especially on author or submitter portals — confirm they are on a build after this fix.
internal.who_should_get_it: All customers; the bug affected every org without the Speaker Feedback feature row, which was effectively every org in production.
internal.gotchas: The per-session feedback/get endpoint still returns 403 if Speaker Feedback is off — that is intentional. Only the flags endpoint was changed to return a graceful empty payload.
internal.talk_track: A recent update caused portal pages to show error banners for events without Speaker Feedback. This fix removes those errors automatically — no settings change or reload needed.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should note that Speaker Feedback must be enabled on the org for the feedback-flags functionality to be active; without it, the portal silently skips the request.
draft.why_use_it: Before this fix, every portal page for events without the Speaker Feedback feature triggered a 403 error from the feedback-flags API call, causing a red "Request failed" toast to appear on every page load for admins and speakers alike. The portal config now checks whether Speaker Feedback is enabled before making that request, so the error never fires. For browser tabs already open when this fix deployed, the flags endpoint now returns a safe empty response instead of a 403, clearing the toasts without requiring a page reload.

entries.title: Public voting shows the round to signed-in visitors who are not eligible, and the ballot count follows the tab
entries.summary: A signed-in visitor who is not on a round’s eligible-voter list sees the plan name and instructions instead of an empty page. On the ballot, the result count matches the **All**, **Voted** or **Not voted** tab you are on.

where.path: Program Site → a public voting round

entries.use_case: Attendees who land on a vote they cannot take still see what it is, instead of assuming the page is broken.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer says some voters see a blank voting page, or the count on the ballot does not match the filter.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers running public voting restricted to an eligible-voter list.
internal.gotchas: Only the round’s public header (plan name, instructions) is shown to an ineligible visitor; no submissions.

entries.title: What's New: a red dot when something is new, and screenshots on each update
entries.summary: A red dot next to **Community** in the sidebar means something has gone live since you last looked, and while it shows, **Community** opens straight onto **What's New**. The feed is now grouped by day (**Today**, **Yesterday**, then the date) with a **New since your last visit** marker, and each card carries its module and two links — **Read the release note** and **How to use it**. Changes that shipped with screenshots or a video show a thumbnail; click it to view them full size and step through. The **Release notes by email** switch sits at the top of the feed.

where.path: Community (sidebar) → What's New

entries.use_case: An admin signs in on Monday, sees the red dot on Community, lands on What's New, reads the three changes from Friday grouped under that date, opens the screenshots of the new dialog without leaving the page, and clicks How to use it for the one that matters to her team.

cs_action.note: Community is on for every admin; nothing to enable.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to keep up with new Sessionboard features, or when onboarding a new admin who wants release notes delivered automatically.
internal.who_should_get_it: Every admin — Community is in the sidebar footer of every organization and event.
internal.gotchas: The dot is per user and clears when What's New is opened; it is driven by the newest release note the sync has seen live or the newest published Console post. The sidebar link only points at What's New while the dot is showing — otherwise Community opens on Ideas as before. The email switch is a plain on/off for signed-in users (login address, no confirmation email); the public Help Center form is the one with double opt-in.
internal.talk_track: When we ship something, Community in your sidebar gets a red dot. Click it and you land on What's New with the changes grouped by day — screenshots right there on the card, and a link to the guide for each one.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should document the red-dot nav indicator, the day-grouped What's New layout, the Media Lightbox (keyboard controls, item counter), and the Release notes by email toggle in both What's New and Account settings.
draft.why_use_it: When Sessionboard ships something new, you now see a red dot on the **Community** sidebar link so you never miss an update. Opening **What's New** clears the dot and shows entries grouped by day, each with a type pill, module label, and any related screenshots or videos you can browse in a full-screen lightbox without leaving the page. Turn on **Release notes by email** once — in **What's New** or in **Account settings** — and each new release note arrives in your inbox automatically, so your whole team can stay informed even when they are not logged in.

entries.title: Invoice reminder history is now visible in Plans & Billing
entries.summary: A new **Billing notices** card under **Invoices** in **Plans & Billing** shows every invoice reminder Sessionboard has sent: when it was sent, which invoice it referenced, every recipient, who triggered it (a named person or "Automatic reminder · before due date / past due"), the balance at the time, and the SendGrid delivery status (**Delivered**, **Opened**, **Bounced**, etc.). Open invoice rows also display a "Reminder sent \<date\>" label. Staff can see the same list per event under **Settings → Billing & Usage**.

where.path: Organization → Plans & Billing → Invoices → Billing notices

entries.use_case: Organizers with billing access can confirm exactly when reminder emails were sent for an outstanding invoice, who received them, and whether they were delivered — useful when following up on overdue payments or resolving disputes about whether a notice was received.

cs_action.note: Visible by default to anyone with View Billing Details. No enablement needed. Staff can also view per-event notices under Event → Settings → Billing & Usage.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer disputes receiving an invoice reminder, or asks for an audit trail of billing communications.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer who manages invoices or has had payment disputes.
internal.staff_path: Event → Settings → Billing & Usage (lists that event's notices under the usage meters)
internal.gotchas: Requires web-api PR #4449 to be deployed first; until then the card shows 'could not be loaded'.
internal.talk_track: You can now show customers exactly when each reminder was sent and whether it landed in the inbox — no more 'I never got that email' disputes.

draft.docs_gap: No existing guide covers Plans & Billing or invoice reminder history; a new guide (or a section in a billing guide) should document the Billing notices card, its columns, and the delivery status values.
draft.why_use_it: When a payment is overdue, you need proof that reminders were actually sent and received. The **Billing notices** card gives you a timestamped, per-recipient record of every invoice reminder — including automatic pre-due and past-due notices — along with the delivery status from the email provider. You can see at a glance whether a reminder bounced or was opened, so you know whether to resend, update an email address, or escalate. The "Reminder sent \<date\>" label on each open invoice row lets you check reminder history without leaving the invoice list.

entries.title: Evaluation plans: points shown as points, reopening keeps dates, safer Apply recommendations
entries.summary: In round-based evaluation plans, points-scored plans show **N pts** instead of a percentage in the monitor, the average line and the printed report. Reopening a plan keeps the round’s review end date. **Apply recommendations** can only select sessions that are in the chosen round, and a failed re-preview clears the old recommendations instead of leaving them applicable. Moving submissions between rounds moves the live ones and names any deleted ones it skipped, and **Add pre-created session** finds a session by `SESS-20`, `sess20` or `20`.

where.path: Program → Evaluation → an evaluation plan → Monitor, Submissions and Rounds tabs

entries.use_case: A program chair running a multi-round, points-scored review can trust the numbers on screen and in print, and cannot apply a stale recommendation to a session that is not in the round.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer sees “%” on a points plan, says reopening a plan moved the review deadline, or cannot apply recommendations to some rows.
internal.who_should_get_it: Sessions 2.0 customers running multi-round evaluation plans.
internal.staff_path: Program → Evaluation → plan → Submissions → Apply recommendations; Rounds tab → Move.
internal.gotchas: Rows outside the selected round are deliberately unselectable for Apply recommendations (a tooltip says why); select-all skips them. A round move returns an error only when every selected submission is deleted.

entries.title: Disclosures and Contracts now require a CSM to enable — self-serve toggle removed
entries.summary: **Disclosures** and **Contracts** have moved from **Preview** (self-serve toggle) to **Beta** (hand-raise) in **Early Access**. Organizers can click **Request access** to express interest, but a Customer Success Manager must enable either feature before it appears in the product.

enable.path: Early Access → Beta → Disclosures / Contracts → Request access; your CSM enables the org feature

where.path: Get started → Early Access → Beta

entries.use_case: Organizers who want Disclosures or Contracts can request access from Early Access; a CSM reviews and enables the feature, ensuring customers get proper onboarding before using these compliance-sensitive tools.

cs_action.note: Customers can no longer flip Disclosures or Contracts on themselves. They submit a hand-raise from Early Access → Beta; a CSM or staff member must enable the feature via the admin console.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks about collecting speaker disclosures or sending contracts, or you see a hand-raise request come in from Early Access.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer with a compliance, legal, or speaker-agreement use case — conferences requiring COI disclosures or events that send speaker contracts.
internal.staff_path: As a super user: the org's Admin settings (/org/<orgId>/settings/admin) → Early Access → turn on Disclosures (feature--credits_disclosure) or Contracts (feature--contracts). Both are staff_only, so a member's bulk org save cannot add or remove them.
internal.gotchas: Orgs that already had either feature on (several did, as Previews) keep it — this only closes new self-serve activation. PUT /organizations/:orgId still returns 200 for a non-staff save; it silently strips both ids and preserves a CSM-enabled row. Until web-ui-v2 #985 reaches prod, the two cards still render the old Preview toggle and the enable call fails — point customers at Request access or enable it for them.
internal.talk_track: Disclosures and Contracts are now a guided Beta — we want to make sure you get the right setup before you go live with legal workflows. Let me walk you through what each feature does and turn it on for you.

draft.docs_gap: Done 2026-10-11: Early Access catalogue lists both under Organization Betas; Disclosures, Contracts and Docusign articles say Request access / CSM enables.
draft.why_use_it: Disclosures and Contracts involve compliance and legal workflows that benefit from a guided setup conversation. By moving these features to Beta, you get a dedicated onboarding touchpoint with your Customer Success Manager before the features are turned on, reducing the risk of misconfiguration. If you are already using either feature, nothing changes — they remain active on your account. New customers can click **Request access** in Early Access to get the conversation started.

entries.title: Mark portal tasks complete or incomplete for many people or sessions at once
entries.summary: Select records and choose **Mark tasks complete** or **Mark tasks incomplete** — from **Assign** in Contacts, or from **More** on the Sessions agenda list and Submissions — then pick the tasks. Large selections are processed in batches, and each change is written to the record’s History.

where.path: CRM → Contacts → select → Assign; Program → Sessions (agenda list) or Submissions → select → More

entries.use_case: When a team collects headshots or agreements outside the portal, it can close those tasks for a whole batch of speakers in one step instead of opening each profile.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer collected something by email and wants the portal checklist to reflect it, or needs to reopen a task for a group.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using portal tasks.
internal.gotchas: Form tasks are excluded — a form is complete when it is submitted. Up to 500 records and 50 tasks per run; History rows are written only where the status actually changed. The single-record toggle on a contact or account profile now also checks permissions and writes History.

entries.title: Saving a session tells you when a field rule could not be applied
entries.summary: When a field rule — such as a **Min/Max Participants** limit — cannot be written on a session save, the session page and side panel say “Saved, but a field rule was not applied” with the reason, instead of a plain “Saved”. The rule’s log records it as **Not applied** with the same reason.

enable.path: Field Rules are turned on by support; then Library → Fields → Field Rules

where.path: Program → a session (profile or side panel) → Save

entries.use_case: A team relying on rules to keep participant limits right knows straight away when a save did not apply one, instead of finding out from a wrong count later.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer says a field rule silently did nothing on some sessions.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using Field Rules, especially participant-limit rules.
internal.gotchas: The session itself is saved; only the rule’s write was refused.

entries.title: The agenda calendar shows sessions when card display includes a role such as Chairperson
entries.summary: Choosing a participant role column — such as **Chairperson** — as a card display field no longer leaves the agenda calendar empty; sessions appear with the role on their cards. Adding, editing or removing a session participant also re-checks which portal that contact belongs in.

where.path: Program → Agenda (Day, Week and Rooms views)

entries.use_case: A scheduler who wants to see who chairs each session on the calendar can do so without losing the calendar.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer’s agenda calendar suddenly showed no sessions after changing card display fields.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers who show participant roles on agenda cards.

entries.title: Language variants: saved translations always show, and bulk fill reaches every text field
entries.summary: **Edit Language Variants** lists every language that has a saved value, even when that field’s per-language switch is off, so translations are not hidden. **Bulk Update** for language values offers every session text field that stores translations, including custom fields, not only the columns showing in the grid.

enable.path: Languages are turned on by support; then Settings → Languages, and Enable variants on each field

where.path: Program → a session → Edit Language Variants; Program → Sessions → select → Bulk Update

entries.use_case: A multilingual event can fill one language across many sessions in one pass and never loses sight of a translation it already entered.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer says a translation disappeared, or a custom field is missing from the language bulk update.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers running events in more than one language.

entries.title: Files dropped onto a portal file request upload
entries.summary: Dragging a file onto a **File Request** task’s drop zone in the portal uploads it, with the same file type, size and safety checks as choosing it with the file picker.

where.path: Portal → a File Request task

entries.use_case: Speakers and sponsors hand over documents the way they expect to, so fewer of them email files instead.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer says participants’ dropped files never arrived.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers collecting documents through portal file requests.

entries.title: A recording linked to a session through Add media shows its transcript and audio on the session
entries.summary: When a recording is linked to a session with **Add media**, the session shows that recording’s transcript and audio.

where.path: Program → a session → Media

entries.use_case: A team that links recordings to sessions by hand gets the transcript on the session too, ready for recaps and clips.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer linked a recording to a session and the transcript did not appear.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers who import recordings into Marketing → Media.

entries.title: Slides: Add title slide finishes in view, and the wizard from Sessions names your selection
entries.summary: The **Add title slide to presentations** dialog in **Marketing → Slides** keeps checking until the job finishes, even if you switch tabs. Opening the Slides wizard from **Sessions → Create** says how many sessions the current filter selected and shows their titles. **Add to gallery** no longer flashes “No galleries can take this media yet” after a successful add.

where.path: Marketing → Slides → Presentations & files → Add title slide to presentations; Program → Sessions → Create → Slides; Add to gallery

entries.use_case: A team adding title slides to a whole program sees the job finish, and knows exactly which sessions a slides run will cover.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer says the title slide dialog sat on “processing”, or the Slides wizard said “All sessions” when they had filtered.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers generating slides or adding title slides to uploaded presentations.
internal.gotchas: With “select all matching” across several pages, chips for sessions not on the loaded page still show the short id.

entries.title: Contracts list and detail now show native e-sign details and signer status; Send dialog previews who will sign
entries.summary: The **Contracts** tab now surfaces native Sessionboard e-sign metadata and an ordered **Signers** list — including each signer's role, name, email, status, and timestamps — directly on the contract list and detail views. Before opening the **Send** dialog, a new preview call resolves who will sign a given template for a given subject, flagging any unresolved roles as editable and surfacing the same validation messages the send action would return.

enable.path: Get started → Early Access → Preview → Contracts

where.path: CRM → Contracts

entries.use_case: Organizers using Sessionboard's native e-sign can see exactly who has signed, viewed, or declined a contract — and catch missing signer information before hitting Send — without leaving the Contracts tab.

cs_action.note: This is API-side work consumed by the companion web-ui-v2 PR; no separate enablement step beyond the Contracts preview flag.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer on the Contracts preview asks how to track who has signed or wants to know why Send is rejecting their template.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using the native Sessionboard e-sign feature (Contracts preview).
internal.gotchas: Native details and signers only appear for Sessionboard native e-sign contracts; DocuSign and manually-uploaded contracts show null for native details. The companion web-ui-v2 PR must also be deployed for the UI to reflect these changes.
internal.talk_track: You can now see every signer's status right on the Contracts tab, and the Send dialog will tell you upfront if any signer information is missing so you can fix it before the contract goes out.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should add a section covering the native Sessionboard e-sign signer roster on the contract list and detail views, and explain the signer preview shown in the Send dialog (editable roles, validation messages).
draft.why_use_it: When you manage contracts natively in Sessionboard, you need to know at a glance whether each required signer has acted and whether the contract is ready to go out. The updated Contracts list and detail view now show each signer's name, role, current status, and key timestamps (viewed, signed, declined) so you can track progress without opening a separate tool. Before you send, the signer preview resolves who will sign a template for a specific contact or pipeline entry and immediately flags any roles that still need a name or email address — giving you a chance to fix problems before the send action rejects them.

entries.title: Marketing Site now has a public session detail page
entries.summary: Each session on a Marketing Site's **Agenda** page now has its own public URL. The page shows session details, speakers (with links to their Site profiles where available), recordings, clips, and the published recap. The page respects embargo settings — while an embargo is active, the description, recap, and embargoed media are withheld. The session URL is picked up by Grip's Summary URL, the Public API, and the Site's sitemap automatically; when an event has multiple Sites, the earliest-published eligible Site owns the canonical URL.

where.path: Site → Agenda → a session

entries.use_case: Organizers who publish a Marketing Site can now send attendees or prospects a direct link to any session — complete with speakers, recordings, clips, and the recap — without building a separate landing page. The page is automatically indexed in the sitemap and picked up by integrations like Grip.

cs_action.note: The org-portal page must be deployed before web-api, then web-ui-v2, then the Cloudflare og-meta Worker — in that order per environment.
